mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.25%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.25% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 10.0%, it signals a severe labor market contraction that triggers policy responses and reduces corporate profit expectations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 10.0 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a deteriorating labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS decline and UNRATE rise does not produce negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market contraction regime (HOUST below 550.0), weak residential construction activity signals reduced consumer confidence and lower economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST < 550.0 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained expansion in industrial production (INDPRO above 100.0) indicates robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO > 100.0 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 570.0, it signals a weakening in the residential sector that reduces consumer spending and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST < 570.0 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 217.5) and unchanged monetary policy (FEDFUNDS <= 0.25%) indicates an inflationary environment without policy response, which erodes real corporate profits and causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of CPIAUCSL > 217.5 and FEDFUNDS <= 0.25 does not produce negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: In a high unemployment regime (UNRATE > 9.5%), the labor market slack reduces consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 9.5 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).
